headline: Go Pointers Explained Simply and with Practical Examples
summary: Learn about pointers in Go, how they work, and why they are essential for efficient memory management and data manipulation.
details: For developers coming from languages like JavaScript, Python, or Java, understanding pointers in Go can be initially daunting due to automatic memory management in those languages.

A pointer is a variable that stores the memory address of another variable, rather than its direct value. The '&' operator finds the address of a variable, while '*' accesses or modifies the value at that address and declares a pointer type.
Pointers are primarily used to work with the same instance of data, avoiding unnecessary copies. For example, a function receiving a user's address can modify the original object directly.
Without pointers, a function would receive a copy of the data, leaving the original unchanged. This distinction is crucial for efficient programming and managing complex data structures.
This guide breaks down the concept of pointers in Go, covering what they are, why they are used, and providing real-world examples to illustrate their practical application.

headline_marked: [[Your AI Slop Bores Me]] lets you roleplay as a chatbot
headline: Your AI Slop Bores Me lets you roleplay as a chatbot
summary: This new web app lets you experience the limitations of AI by having humans roleplay as chatbots, complete with a 150-second response time and a basic drawing tool.
details: Your AI Slop Bores Me is a novel web application that allows users to engage in a unique form of AI interaction. The platform features two main modes: 'human' and 'LARP as an AI'. In either mode, users can submit requests or respond to them, but with a twist – a human is on the other side.

Requests can be for text or image responses, and the person roleplaying as the AI has a strict 150-second time limit to reply. This constraint, combined with a rudimentary MS-Paint-like drawing tool for image requests, simulates the challenges and limitations faced by actual AI models.

Similar to real LLMs, the platform operates on a credit system. Users earn credits by answering requests themselves when in the AI role, or they can wait two minutes for a free request. This encourages active participation and provides a hands-on understanding of AI response generation.

While many users request drawings of obscure anime characters or engage in other creative prompts, the core fun lies in the challenge of maintaining the illusion of being an AI under extreme time and tool limitations. Users can also skip requests that don't appeal to them.

The platform also boasts a Discord server and a 'Hall of Fame' showcasing impressive user-generated content, including a notable rendition of Starry Night. Despite some obtrusive ads, the app offers a humorous and insightful look into the world of AI interaction.
